review_findings: Five test methods cover O0/O2 and debug/nondebug; integer widths/signs, duplicate values and high unsigned bits,32+32 spans,15/16/17 left-span boundaries, a one-element right span, comparator>/>= and renamed/right-first exclusive comparisons.

Fresh V8 and Python Wasmtime instances receive forged public slice headers. An independent ordered scalar memory model checks return/trap and observed memory windows; optional frozen-reference execution compares complete engine records including abort callbacks. The dynamic cases include overlapping sources/destination, short logical bounds, negative cursors, huge endpoints, high and wrapping pointers, and partial physical writes.

Address-exposed/captured views and extra side effects are negative matcher cases. With the reference option, negative/debug function bodies must remain byte-identical and eligible O2 bodies must change.

Ordinary fixture output also matches native Goose; native runs do not receive the forged-memory scenarios. Final source cursor values are not directly exported by this fixture; output cursor, memory and subsequent comparisons exercise cursor behavior indirectly.

The retained runtime regression exercises a Wasm start function with current-request input, initialized memory, start traps, invalid-input callback failure and recovery on reused module/fresh instances. It changes no production host behavior.
